newsitem.title: USA: US Northeast spot power prices rise on cold spell.
newsitem.headline: US Northeast spot power prices rise on cold spell.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. rose Monday in line with those in the rest of the country, which is experiencing the worst cold spell so far this winter season.

Despite clear skies, the region was enveloped in a cold, windy system that brought sub-zero degree Fahrenheit temperatures to some areas. By Friday, another Arctic cold blast could drag temperatures in the Northeast even lower.
Although utilities needed to switch on expensive oil/gas generation to meet peak electricity demand, off-peak usage remained well-supplied by coal and nuclear generation, market sources said.
"You have an abundance of off-peak power available," said a New York power trader.
Hourly dispatch rates in the Northeast during today's peak demand periods was talked as high as $45.00-$50.00 per megawatt hour (MWh).

Peak, non-firm electricity prices (including transmission costs) for Tuesday delivery in the eastern part of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) jumped to $32.00-$35.00/MWh from Friday's $31.00-$32.00 for Monday delivery.
Off-peak, non-firm power for next-day delivery in eastern NYPP increased to $22.00-$24.00 from Friday's quote of $22.00.

In western NYPP, peak, non-firm power for Tuesday firmed to $28.00-$29.00 from Friday's $26.00-$27.00/MWh in tandem with higher prices in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect power pool, where day-ahead power jumped two to three dollars from Friday.
Western NYPP electricity for off-peak, non-firm delivery Tuesday remained steady at $15.00-$16.00.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for day-ahead delivery at Northeast Utilities' (NU) border climbed to $35.00-$36.00 from $34.00-$35.00 Friday for Monday delivery.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for next-day delivery to the NU border rose to $23.00-$26.00 from Friday's $22.00.

Swing natural gas prices rose sharply on outlook of extreme cold in the region through the end of the week. Next-day gas deliveries at the New York City gate surged to the $5.00 per million British thermal unit level, up 50 cents from Friday.
